novelty: NOVEL. NOT in README.md or SECURITY.md: SECURITY.md scope names secret-read/approval-forgery/policy-change/cross-user-socket, not availability of the broker. README 'What envh does not do' acknowledges bearer-token session reuse, same-user show/clipboard, the unlock-hour, X11/uinput/tmux, 'approve a command line not the code', and under 'Not provided: ... rate limits ...' -- but that 'rate limits' sits beside 'per-request network allow-lists' and 'remote use', i.e. provider/network-side throttling of key USE, not the control socket's own anti-abuse caps. The README's session-id discussion (README.md:400, 'about 36,000 ids') is framed purely around GUESSING (confidentiality) and never says a user can create unbounded sessions or that filling the id namespace wedges the broker. The broker in fact implements several socket anti-abuse caps (MAX_PENDING_PER_USER=20 state.py:131, MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_UID=32 control.py:28, MAX_UNKNOWN_SESSION_IDS=20 broker.py:40, V4 reason cap), so the missing live-session cap is an oversight, not an acknowledged design limit. NOT a re-derivation of V1-V8: V1=alias repr() DoS, V2=oversized-YAML wedge, V3=fd-exhaustion/idle-timeout (a DIFFERENT resource -- open connections/fds, mitigated by MAX_CONNECTIONS + FIRST_LINE_TIMEOUT; this attack closes every connection so it never trips those caps), V4=reason disk-fill, V5=duration overflow, V6=import oracle, V7=per-user id count leak, V8=hook bypasses. This is a new exhaustion class (session-id namespace) that no V1-V8 fix covers. World novelty: public prior art exists (CWE-770 allocation without limits/throttling, CWE-799 uncontrolled resource consumption, CWE-331 insufficient entropy / fixed id space, OWASP ASVS V11 anti-automation, ATT&CK T1499/.004 endpoint DoS); the project docs simply never named this instance.

reasoning: Root cause is the conjunction of three source facts, all verified on this instance (commit 90f42862). (1) FIXED, UNDERSIZED ID SPACE: session ids are adjective-noun pairs drawn from src/envh/core/words.py, 176 adjectives x 204 nouns = 35904 possible ids. (2) UNBOUNDED, NON-FALLBACK GENERATOR: src/envh/core/state.py:198-202 _new_session_id() is `while True: candidate=...choice(ADJECTIVES)-...choice(NOUNS); if candidate not in self.sessions: return candidate`. self.sessions (state.py:100) holds EVERY session -- live, ended, and expired-but-unpruned (only prune_history() at state.py:185-196 deletes from it, 1h after expiry). Once 35904 distinct ids are present, the `not in` condition is unsatisfiable and the loop never terminates. There is no retry cap and no fallback to a wider id (e.g. token_hex). (3) NO LIVE-SESSION CAP: state.py:204 create_session and broker.py:214-242 request_session cap nothing on the number of simultaneously-live sessions; state.py:131 caps only PENDING requests, and an auto-granted canary session (needs_approval False -> _announce_or_grant auto-approves, broker.py:126-132) is decided at once, so it never counts toward the pending cap. control.py:27-28 connection caps (MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_UID=32) limit only concurrently OPEN connections; the attack opens-and-closes one connection per session, so it stays far under them. WEDGE MECHANISM: the arena broker (redteam/.../arena/serve_broker.py) and production (src/envh/server/serve.py) both run a SINGLE-THREADED asyncio loop (asyncio.run), and _new_session_id / create_session are synchronous (no await, no run_in_executor/to_thread). The moment the 35905th session_start enters the full-table loop, the whole event loop is pinned and every other client -- including a different user and the console -- is frozen; the sweeper that calls prune_history() (serve_broker.py:66 create_task + :64) is an asyncio task ON THE SAME loop, so it can never run to reclaim ids. The wedge is therefore permanent and unrecoverable without restarting the broker. A single non-root listed user (rt1) reaches it headlessly because the AUTO_CANARY `canary` preset is auto-granted with no approver. Reproduced: filled to exactly 35904 ids; rt2 `status` then received NO reply for a full 20s client window (healthy control: 0.05s), and a fresh rt1 `session_start` on the wedged instance hung with no reply for its full 15s window. VERDICT CONFIRMED / HIGH: in scope (non-root socket client), independently reproduced with pasted output, real and reliable broker-wide DoS (Sec4 DoS win condition, 'wedging its event loop / exhausting it'), and novel (not README/SECURITY, not V1-V8; the V3 fd/connection-exhaustion fix does not cover the session-id namespace). Severity HIGH per Sec6 = reliable DoS.
recommended_fix: Cap simultaneously-live sessions per-uid and globally in create_session/request_session, AND bound _new_session_id with a retry limit that falls back to a wide random id (e.g. secrets.token_hex) when the word-pair space is near-full, so a full table can never spin the loop.
